name: The Holm Oak of Piazza Perin del Vaga

location.address: Piazza Perin del Vaga, Della Vittoria/Flaminio district
location.neighbourhood: Della Vittoria (RAMI's own field note says quartiere Flaminio; the piazza sits on the boundary, so give both if the writer wants to hedge)

verified_sources: MASAF national register / Lazio regional register, sheet 63/H501/RM/12 (girth 280 cm, height 18 m, criteria: form and bearing; historical, cultural or religious value)

https://ilregistrodeglialberi.it/17724-tutta-roma-leccio-roma-rm-lazio (RAMI entry #17724, AMI code 63/H501/RM/12 matches the register sheet exactly; coordinates 41.925194,12.464699 match to the metre; girth 2.80 m and height 18.00 m match; registered 17/11/2025; health 'Buona'; accessibility 'Accessibile'; estimated age ~126 years calculated from the registered birth year, i.e. planted around 1900)
transport: In the residential Della Vittoria/Flaminio district, roughly 15-20 minutes' walk from Piazzale Flaminio or Lepanto (Metro A)
verify_notes: Two independent sources agree closely: MASAF/Lazio register sheet 63/H501/RM/12 and RAMI's own field survey (entry #17724, 'Tutta Roma'), same AMI code, coordinates matching within metres, girth and height matching almost exactly (280cm/18m vs 2.80m/18.00m). RAMI's field note gives the story hook: children who used to climb the tree would shout 'Anvedi da quassu se vede tutta Roma' (look, from up here you can see all of Rome), which gave the tree its RAMI nickname 'Tutta Roma'. It was already standing and being climbed around 1919, and RAMI's own age calculation from the registered birth year puts planting at roughly 1900, so roughly 126 years old as of the November 2025 survey (call it 125-130 now). Registered on Italy's national monumental tree list in October 2025, criteria form/bearing plus historical-cultural-religious value, which is unusual among Rome's register entries (most are registered for size alone) and points at a genuine local story rather than a merely large tree. Health assessed 'Buona' (good) as of the 17/11/2025 survey, accessibility rated 'Accessibile'. Isolated from every other published Rome cluster (Della Vittoria/Flaminio, north of the centre near the Tiber), so this would open a new, single-tree waypoint rather than thicken an existing walk; note that for whoever plans the city's walks next, it does not have to gate publication. No photo found in this pass (photo hunting is out of scope for a verification pass).

name: The Hackberry of the Parco degli Scipioni

location.address: Parco degli Scipioni, Via di Porta Latina 16
location.neighbourhood: Via Appia / Porta Latina, near the Aurelian Walls

verified_sources: MASAF national register / Lazio regional register, sheet 66/H501/RM/12 (girth 401 cm, height 20 m)

https://www.parcoappiaantica.it/il-territorio/alberi-di-pregio-appia-antica/ (Parco Regionale dell'Appia Antica's own 'alberi di pregio' catalogue: Parco degli Scipioni, Via di Porta Latina 16, height 15 m, circumference 400 cm, estimated age ~100 years, stato fitosanitario Buono; described as integrated into Raffaele de Vico's 1931 landscape design and as one of the park's most important specimens for its dimensions, bearing and balanced canopy)
access: Free, public park within the Parco Regionale dell'Appia Antica, standard park hours (roughly 7am to sunset)
transport: Entrance at Via di Porta Latina 16, near Porta Latina in the Aurelian Walls; roughly 20-25 minutes' walk from Circo Massimo (Metro B), or reachable by bus along Via Appia Antica
verify_notes: Two independent sources: the MASAF/Lazio register (sheet 66/H501/RM/12, girth 401cm, height 20m) and the Parco Regionale dell'Appia Antica's own 'alberi di pregio' page, which names this exact tree at Via di Porta Latina 16 with matching girth (400cm) but a lower height figure (15m vs the register's 20m). FLAGGED for that height disagreement; do not silently pick a winner, state both if the story needs a height. The park authority's own health assessment reads 'Stato fitosanitario: Buono' (good), which is real vitality evidence beyond the register. Story hook: planted as part of Raffaele de Vico's 1929/1931 layout of the park around the Tomb of the Scipios and the columbarium of Pomponius Hylas, a few steps from the Aurelian Walls; the park authority calls it 'una maestosa cellula' distinguished by size, bearing and a balanced crown, and one of the park's most important specimens. A near-identical second hackberry (Lazio sheet 65/H501/RM/12, 414cm girth, at 41.876361,12.502667, described in the register as standing against the Aurelian wall itself at the corner of Via Latina, about 110m away) remains register-only after two verify passes; it is left in leads rather than shipped as a pair since no independent source names it individually and it would be dishonest to imply both are equally corroborated. If the writer wants a two-tree Scipioni/Mura Latine moment, this is the one tree of the pair that actually clears the bar today. No photo found in this pass.
